Master Series - Sales Strategies.title: Stop Leaking GP$
Master Series - Sales Strategies.tags: Sales, Selling, Strategy, Gross Profit, James DeVito, profitability, margins, revenue, pricing, efficiency, performance, finance, operations, metrics, growth, discipline, management, strategy, accountability, business
Master Series - Sales Strategies.description: A little here, a little there - small leaks aren't always taken seriously because they seem...well, small at the time. But when it comes to profitability, leaking GP$ throughout an entire month can add up to significant loss. This loss directly affects the bottom line and, in turn, your income as an advisor. Stopping the leaks and capturing these GP$ is something all service advisors should be paying attention to.

Master Series - Sales Strategies.title: Don't Be Afraid of the Truth
Master Series - Sales Strategies.tags: Sales, Selling, Strategy, Trust, Fear, James DeVito, honesty, transparency, integrity, trust, credibility, communication, professionalism, relationships, confidence, accountability, ethics, service, customers, reputation, authenticity
Master Series - Sales Strategies.description: So, the truth…I find that the truth can cause advisors to stumble sometimes...or a lot of the time. Can the truth kinda suck sometimes? Yes, but we don’t want to be that friend who tells our best friend that their voice sounds amazing and to go on American Idol when that’s the last thing they should do. They NEED to hear the truth. But is it going to make them cry and be mad at you or see the light and appreciate that they have someone in their life willing to tell them how it is without making them feel stupid and dumb?

Master Series - Sales Strategies.title: Assume the Sale
Master Series - Sales Strategies.tags: Sales, Selling, Strategy, James DeVito, closing, confidence, psychology, engagement, mindset, conversations, influence, decisions, trust, communication, strategy, persuasion, commitment, performance, sales
Master Series - Sales Strategies.description: Assuming the Sale is a way of speaking with your customers that assumes they are going to buy from you today. Something that I tell my classes when they are going through the certification process is - Did you know that your customers actually expect to spend money when they come into your shop, into this place of business? How MUCH money depends on you. They came in for that rattle but will they also buy the 80K Service they’re due for? It’s like a restaurant server - This dinner group is planning to spend money and they for sure want the main course. But will they also buy apps, dessert, or another drink? The server has a huge influence on that decision. (you'll definitely want to leave some room for our desert special tonight, it’s amazing.). For us as service advisors, there are of course a lot of ways to influence that. The mindset and execution of Assuming the Sale is just one of them.

Esepcially when many of the options available in auto repair are interest free for a period of time. Master Series - Sales Strategies.tags: Sales, Selling, Strategy, Fear, Kyle Martin, confidence, mindset, communication, courage, growth, trust, resilience, performance, opportunities, professionalism, engagement, customers, success, development
Master Series - Sales Strategies.description: As it relates to sales, fear is very often caused by what we think the other person IS thinking, WILL think, or WANTS to think. Assumptions and presumptions become the driving forces behind our fear. Compounding that can be any number of other fears - fear of failure, of making a mistake, of causing conflict...the list goes on and on. As these fears stack, the chances of losing the sale increase. Customers have their own fears when it comes to trusting an advisor. If we can't overcome our own fears, helping a customer get past theirs is much more difficult. Identifying our fears is the first step to overcoming them.

Master Series - Sales Strategies.title: Phone Scripts and Call Conversions
Master Series - Sales Strategies.tags: Sales, Selling, Strategy, Scripts, Kyle Martin, calls, conversions, communication, confidence, engagement, listening, trust, professionalism, responses, relationships, appointments, customers

Having a plan for your phone calls isn't meant to stifle your natural charisma or stop you from being...well, YOU. Its simply recognizing what has worked in the past to convert customers and what hasn't. Want to stay way from unnecessary tangents? Use scripts. Want to get more time back in your day? Use scripts. Want to more easily convert customers from asking questions to saying YES? Use scripts. When used well, scripts help you in more ways than you may realize. Getting that phone to ring costs a lot of marketing dollars and your team is relying on you to convert those calls to sales. Scripts can help you do that.

Master Series - Sales Strategies.title: Winning with Third-Party Warranties
Master Series - Sales Strategies.tags: Sales, Selling, Strategy, Warranty, Mike Tatich, warranties, coverage, communication, approvals, trust, advocacy, education, expectations, relationships, transparency, confidence, service, customers, solutions, value
Master Series - Sales Strategies.description: Such a headache, a waste of time, interrupts the whole process' ... But - like waiter oil changes - if you approach third party warranties from a position of integrating it into your processes instead of pushing against it, then there's a lot to gain. But you need to be prepared, you need to have a strategy, and you need to want to help your customer win. Not every sale comes easy. And if you can help your customer win, you win.

Then the sales call does end up being short and neither the customer or the shop win. In this workshop we'll break down the ticket prep process to give you an easy way to never miss a beat when presenting to your customers by empowering you to always feel like you have OPTIONS.

Master Series - Sales Strategies.tags: Sales, Selling, Finance, Mike Tatich, financing, affordability, approvals, payments, communication, confidence, flexibility, solutions, accessibility, trust, value, engagement, customers, growth
Master Series - Sales Strategies.description: Would you like to pay for that t-shirt with 10 easy payments of $2? EVERYTHING can be financed now. That may be one of the more comical examples but easy financing options have become something people are used to. So why don't auto repair shops talk about it more? Why don't advisor's incorporate it more into their sales strategy? Waiting until a financial objection is presented isn't the only way to utilize financing. When done strategically, your ARO will increase and your customer will leave with a more reliable vehicle.

The more customized the solution, the more helpful it is for you to have a plan. Good processes, good scripts, and having the right mindset can all assist in helping you sell to any budget. Because every budget has a solution.

Master Series - Sales Strategies.tags: Price, pricing, phone, quoting, sales, strategy, Leann Dennis, communication, value, diagnostics, trust, expectations, transparency, education, conversations, confidence, recommendations, customers, service
Master Series - Sales Strategies.description: There are countless reasons why you don't want to give prices over the phone. If you don't have a plan for how you are going to communicate to those would-be customers, then they will become never-are customers. This lesson will focus on how to be prepared for these calls - every single time - and how being successful with curb selling requires more than just good scripts. Oftentimes, it's more about you than it is the customer.

Master Series - Sales Strategies.tags: good, bad, news, mindset, selling, Mike Tatich, communication, empathy, transparency, trust, professionalism, expectations, confidence, relationships, listening, credibility, conversations, customers, service, resilience

As an advisor you can be empathetic and lead your customer through a decision making process at the same time. And it all starts with your mindset.

Master Series - Sales Strategies.tags: No, Responding, Sales, Mike Tatich, objections, responses, communication, trust, confidence, engagement, listening, relationships, persistence, professionalism, influence, conversations, customers, strategy
Master Series - Sales Strategies.description: When a customer tells you no, how are you prepared to respond? How you answer that question will determine your success as an advisor. It's our obligation as service advisors to help customers see things from additional perspectives that shines new light on how to prioritize their vehicles needs. In turn, this also changes how they prioritize their budget. But you need them to want to hear what you have say if you're ever going help them get to that point.

Master Series - Sales Strategies.title: Stop Order Taking. Start Curb Selling Like a Trusted Advisor
Master Series - Sales Strategies.tags: Melanie Schambach, advising, trust, communication, recommendations, relationships, engagement, credibility, education, value, professionalism, confidence, customers, service, influence, sales
Master Series - Sales Strategies.description: Curb selling isn’t just about saying "Yes". It’s about how you lead the conversation before the customer ever walks through the door. Many service advisors fall into the role of an order taker, giving answers and leaving decisions up to the customer. Trusted advisors do it differently. They guide the conversation with strategic questions, clear options, and confident direction. In this session, you’ll learn how to guide the conversation so your customers feel confident in their decision, not unsure when they hang up.

Master Series - Sales Strategies.tags: Leann Dennis, maintenance, inspections, value, education, communication, opportunities, awareness, recommendations, trust, engagement, prevention, customers, service, retention, growth
Master Series - Sales Strategies.description: Most service advisors treat coupon oil changes like a quick, low-value transaction, but what if that mindset is costing you thousands? Because the truth is, many of these customers are trying you out for the very first time, and how you show up determines whether they ever come back or buy more than just the coupon oil change. If you’re ready to stop “processing” oil changes and start converting them into real revenue, this session will show you why it’s so important to impress every time to increase revenue.

Master Series - Sales Strategies.tags: James DeVito, priorities, needs, wants, communication, value, trust, engagement, understanding, relationships, influence, recommendations, decisions, customers, strategy, sales

They come into the shop with what they want (their main concern), we then find what the additional items they need (through an inspection), and... it stops there. How do we turn what they need into what they want?

Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.tags: Leadership, Growth, Mindset, Work, Life, Kyle Martin, balance, wellbeing, priorities, health, productivity, relationships, planning, fulfillment, focus, energy, motivation, lifestyle, success, happiness
Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.description: Your professional work and your personal life do not exist at the sacrifice of one another. Yes, there are times when one requires more of your focus and/or time than the other but winning in one area can, and should, support you winning in the other area. Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.title: The Limitations of Comfort
Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.tags: Leadership, Growth, Mindset, Comfort, James DeVito, limitations, courage, challenges, confidence, development, adaptability, resilience, opportunities, improvement, success, progress
Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.description: Stalling out, complacency, "hitting your ceiling" ... these are all different ways to describe when someone has hit their limit or created self-imposed limitations. What is the balance between overworking and working to your full potential? When we get too comfortable, not only does it limit us from reaching our potential but it (unfairly) limits those around us as well. Being able to recognize when this is happening and take steps to correct it will not only help your sales but can also save your career.

Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.title: Fearless Attitude of the Conversation
Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.tags: Leadership, Growth, Mindset, Attitude, Leann Dennis, fearlessness, confidence, communication, courage, trust, engagement, conversations, professionalism, influence, resilience, relationships, customers, sales, success
Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.description: Your customers need to hear what you have to say. So, the conversation that needs to be had is inevitable. Knowing what you should say, how to say it, and how to customize it to your surroundings are the keys to finding the confidence you need to be fearless in those conversations. Whether its over the phone or in person, in front of coworkers or even other customers, how can you remove hesitation and replace it with purpose?

Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.title: Building Trust for High Performance Teams
Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.tags: Leadership, Growth, Mindset, Attitude, Trust, Team, Teamwork, Kyle Martin, collaboration, accountability, communication, culture, relationships, engagement, performance, credibility, respect, success, professionalism
Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.description: As the old quote goes, "Trust is a two way street." There's another quote though that can't be forgotten: "Trust doesn't come easy." This can be especially true in a shop between advisors and technicians. No one wants to let their guard down; everyone is scared of backing down and "losing." Being vulnerable enough to allow honesty in the conversation is where you start building trust. Sometimes this honesty can create temporary conflict but it's through that conflict where trust is earned, collaboration begins, and ultimately, strong teams are built.

Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.title: Shop Employee vs. Shop Representative
Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.tags: Leadership, Growth, Mindset, James DeVito, representation, professionalism, accountability, ownership, communication, reputation, responsibility, engagement, culture, credibility, service, customers, performance
Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.description: Every interaction you have with your customers is a reflection of your shop's goals & ethos and whether or not you are bought in with them. This goes beyond branding and beyond being the face of the company. It gets to the root of poor mindsets like "not my customer," "they weren't going to buy anyways," "sorry, it's just company policy, my hands are tied," ... the list goes on. The more you see yourself as just an employee, the less you will care - the shorter you'll be with customers on the phone, the less you'll try, and the bare minimum will become your standard. When you have someone else (the company) to blame, there's no reason to have any pride. Pride comes with ownership and being your shop's representative.

Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.tags: Technician, growth, Mike Tatich, conflict, communication, technicians, teamwork, collaboration, professionalism, relationships, accountability, leadership, trust, respect, problemsolving, culture, service, performance
Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.description: To be clear, the same could be said about advisor's. Ask any technician and they'll tell you as much. For a multitude of possible reasons, some people just don't like to make it easy to work alongside them. But just like you can ask any technician about that, you can ask any advisor about difficult technicians and they'll also have a story to tell. And the interesting thing is: the more you hear the stories, the more you come to discover similarities across them all. And you discover that the solution that worked for them could very likely work for you. While not always easy, building a working relationship with your technicians will result in more sales for you, more hours for them, and an overall more efficient shop.

If you want to learn how to get the most out of a small shop, join us for this interview with Ashley Wright of Premier Auto Repair!

Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.title: How to Have Tough Conversations with Leadership
Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.tags: Conversation, Hard, Leadership, Leann Dennis, communication, feedback, professionalism, accountability, trust, relationships, courage, transparency, conflict, respect, collaboration, growth, workplace, development
Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.description: Being a service advisor is a hard job. And hard things sometimes require hard conversations. Perhaps it's related to teamwork in the shop or maybe its about the customer experience. It could even be about yourself. Whatever the case, when you think something needs attention - especially if its limiting your performance - its time for a conversation with leadership. How you go about planning for and having that conversation is the difference between it being productive or you feeling like nothing got accomplished.

Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.title: C.O.N.F.I.D.E.N.C.E.
Master Series - Leadership & Personal Gr.tags: Confidence, growth, Mike Tatich, mindset, communication, courage, trust, professionalism, resilience, engagement, leadership, performance, belief, success, development, achievement

Building a team where everyone understands how their individual goals are part of larger goals allows for better communication, problem solving, and leads to a squad that knows how to find solutions that don't discount any one persons individual goals.

Master Series - Processes & Organization.title: Sales Special Opps - Part 3

Master Series - Processes & Organization.description: Embracing imperfect situations as a means to find the solution is a key step in forming a team that knows how to move forward. Conflict between team members can happen as a result of many things in a repair shop. Whatever the cause is, meeting it head on to find quick resolution is paramount. Days in a repair shop won't always be perfect. If you don't have a plan for handling conflict, it will cause chaos. If you can embrace the conflict as the only way forward, you'll create an unstoppable team.

Master Series - Processes & Organization.title: Sales as a Creative Process
Master Series - Processes & Organization.tags: Process, Processes, Organize, Organization, Creative, Sales, James DeVito, creativity, communication, problemsolving, innovation, engagement, trust, relationships, value, influence, adaptability, confidence, customers, strategy, sales, growth
Master Series - Processes & Organization.description: The "creative process" is most commonly referred to when talking about artists, writers, designers, and practitioners of other such endeavors. But you don't hear about it in sales quite as much. There's a lot to be said about the benefits of structure in the sales process - we've covered a lot of it in our certification course. But there are a lot of lessons we can learn as service advisors from what goes into a creative process like those mentioned. The more creative you can be in your sales, the more likely you are to find solutions.

Master Series - Processes & Organization.title: Nailing Your Check-In Process
Master Series - Processes & Organization.tags: Process, Processes, Organize, Organization, Check In, Nailing, Melanie Schambach, checkin, workflow, communication, expectations, professionalism, trust, efficiency, engagement, consistency, preparation, customers, service, experience, success
Master Series - Processes & Organization.description: In order to solve issues farther down the line in a given process, the best place to start is very often at the beginning. It's never a bad time to review the building blocks of your customers experience. When looked at from one angle, everything seems fine. But from a different angle, there's missing blocks. And when your process is only as strong as the last weakest point, what does that say for your customer experience when the weakest point is at the beginning?

Master Series - Processes & Organization.title: Generating Opportunities: When the phones go silent...
Master Series - Processes & Organization.tags: Process, Processes, Organize, Organization, Slow, Phone, Phones, Callback, Opportunities, Generating, Silent, Leann Dennis, outreach, followup, communication, engagement, retention, relationships, productivity, initiative, growth, customers, service, strategy, sales, activity
Master Series - Processes & Organization.description: Phone not ringing? Guess its time to put your feet up and take a break...wrong! It's time to start chasing those leads. When the sales stop coming to you, you have to go find them. Many advisor's don't do callbacks because they see it as "cold calling." Being successful with callbacks isn't just about the call itself but also what happened with that customer on the day of their visit. What they were told and what expectations they were given. You have a role to play when the phones slow down and when you take action the right way, you can still provide a win for both you and your customers.

Master Series - Processes & Organization.title: Proper Repair Order Documentation
Master Series - Processes & Organization.tags: Customer, Experience, Repair, Order, Documentation, Process, Mike Tatich, accuracy, clarity, communication, records, consistency, workflow, professionalism, details, organization, expectations, service, customers, efficiency
Master Series - Processes & Organization.description: Seems basic, right? Well, not necessarily. The repair order is (read: should be) a comprehensive document that provides all information about that visit to anyone who reads it. Not your ticket but you need to provide an answer to a customer? Reference the RO. Technician needs to look back at a car from 5 months ago and see what was done? Reference the RO. Repair orders are about more than customer info/vehicle info/concern. They tell a story - both right now and in the future. Quality repair orders lead to quality invoices, which is the last thing your customers see. The last opportunity to leave them with a good impression. Take time to create a quality repair order and your work will become easier.

Master Series - Processes & Organization.title: Setting Ourselves, Technicians and Customers up for Success!
Master Series - Processes & Organization.tags: Process, Processes, Organize, Organization, Procedure, Success, Technicians, Leann Dennis, preparation, teamwork, communication, expectations, collaboration, trust, workflow, efficiency, customers, service, consistency, performance
Master Series - Processes & Organization.description: It's easy to lose sight of the big picture when selling. Advisors focus on whether or not they're going to be successful and forget that it's not just about them. In our industry and in particular independent repair shops, everyone wins and loses together. Including the customer. And because 1) you're connected to it all and 2) you are the professional communicator ... it's up to you to be the leader when it comes to the setup. Do it right, with everyone in mind, and you'll help everyone find success at the end of the process.

Master Series - Processes & Organization.title: A Proper Check-in Procedure
Master Series - Processes & Organization.tags: Process, Check in, Procedure, Mike Tatich, checkin, communication, workflow, expectations, professionalism, organization, trust, efficiency, engagement, consistency, preparation, customers, service, experience, success
Master Series - Processes & Organization.description: Some topics provide more to talk about than you might think and your check-in process is one of those topics. It isn't just about the vehicle and customer information. It's about setting yourself up for the best chance at getting the sale while also setting your customer up for the best experience they've ever had at a repair shop.

Master Series - Processes & Organization.title: Keeping FOH Frustrations Out of BOH
Master Series - Processes & Organization.tags: Front of house, back of house, FOH, BOH, Frustration, Mike Tatich, communication, teamwork, collaboration, culture, professionalism, respect, relationships, workflow, accountability, technicians, advisors, conflict, efficiency, performance, trust
Master Series - Processes & Organization.description: Front of House and Back of House both have their own frustrations and problems to solve on a day-to-day basis. Stacking ours on top of theirs or theirs on top of ours is not helpful and in fact, can lead to a breakdown in processes, quality of service, and overall disfunction in a shop. You shouldn't let the FOH frustrations become frustrations for the BOH. Protect your team to protect The Win.

Master Series - Processes & Organization.title: Simplicity of the RO
Master Series - Processes & Organization.tags: Simplicity, RO, repair order, process, Leann Dennis, repairorders, clarity, communication, documentation, efficiency, workflow, organization, consistency, accuracy, professionalism, service, customers, process, effectiveness
Master Series - Processes & Organization.description: Your job as a service advisor isn't just to be a "car stuff" translator for your customer, it's also to simplify what can otherwise be very confusing information. If the organization of the RO is causing you to get confused, it will definitely cause your customer to be confused. If you find yourself reading off an endless list of items...if you find yourself short selling (pushing off) items on a ticket because you think it's too much more to talk about...if you find yourself talking in circles and forgetting things...then you need to bring more simplicity to the RO.

Master Series - Processes & Organization.title: The 4-Touch Process for the Clients Next Visit
Master Series - Processes & Organization.tags: 4 touch, Client, Visit, Process, Mike Tatich, followup, retention, communication, engagement, loyalty, relationships, consistency, touchpoints, planning, scheduling, customers, service, strategy, growth, experience
Master Series - Processes & Organization.description: Being an advisor isn't just about the sale TODAY. It's about thinking long term and setting yourself up for future opportunity with your clients. It's not expected that every customer will be able to say yes to everything their car needs. Which means a large majority of your customer leave with recommendations. Beyond a single call-back, how can you engage with them to make the future approval of those recommendations is easy and, more importantly, a reality.

Master Series - Processes & Organization.description: Join Sales Fix trainer Mike Tatich for Chaos Is Expensive. If your workflow feels chaotic, your KPIs are likely feeling it too. You’ll learn why conversion starts before the car ever arrives and how the first few hours of the day can either create space for approvals or close the window entirely. We’ll explore how proactive updates, inspection priority, dispatch alignment, and buying time in the workflow protect both revenue and retention. Chaos doesn’t just make the day harder — it costs you. This webinar will show you how to take back control in a practical, sustainable way. (edited)

Master Series - Customer Experience.description: I have a bad habit of over explaining things." ... "I have a bad habit of talking too fast." ... "I have a bad habit of sounding bland." For better or worse, we all have habits that relate to how we communicate. Many of you have worked hard to overcome bad habits and replace them with good ones. Over time, it can be easy to fall back into those old habits - oftentimes without realizing it. The SMALLEST changes to how we communicate can have the BIGGEST impact for our customers and on our opportunity to win at getting the sale. The more you focus on this, it will evolve from being a habit into being a skillset. And a skillset is something you can work to master.

Master Series - Customer Experience.title: Customer Retention Through Hospitality in Automotive

Master Series - Customer Experience.description: Beyond customer service, beyond the "no update update", there's an opportunity to truly connect with your customers to have such an impact that it resonates long after they've left your shop. Taking care of your customers is paramount if you want to be their long term resource for automotive needs. And when an entire industry exists for the sole purpose of taking care of people - hospitality - we can take some cues.

Master Series - Customer Experience.description: What keeps someone coming back? What makes them hope that you're there when they arrive? Master Series - Customer Experience.description: Customer service in and of itself can be a weaving path of ups and downs over the course of day. How do you stop, pause, restart, present, and sell each job from a clean slate without being impeded by all the interactions that came before it? Master Series - Customer Experience.title: The Fiduciary Responsibility of an Advisor

Are you just a sales person or are you their automotive fiduciary with an obligation to inform them of their vehicles needs, for their benefit? Earn their trust by successfully communicating both their wants AND their needs.

Master Series - Customer Experience.tags: Customer, Experience, Hospitality, Melanie Schambach, excellence, service, loyalty, engagement, trust, professionalism, relationships, satisfaction, reputation, customers, retention, value, growth
Master Series - Customer Experience.description: Just fixing the car right isn't enough if you want long term, repeat customers. There are emotions attached to spending money and its up to service advisors to try and guide customers to stay positive. How do you do that? Give your customers a red carpet experience. The customer service side of auto repair has leveled up across the industry in recent years. What are YOU doing to make sure you stand out amongst the competition and to make sure your customers are well taken care of? When you go above and beyond for your customers, objections disappear and they will allow you to help them solve their problems.

Master Series - Customer Experience.tags: Customer, Experience, Brand, Teamwork, Melanie Schambach, branding, consistency, professionalism, reputation, communication, culture, identity, trust, engagement, perception, relationships, service, customers, excellence, growth
Master Series - Customer Experience.description: We've said this before in our training videos but it bears repeating: You are the face of your company. And your companies brand isn't just a logo or the font type on marketing materials; it's the experience that your company is promising your customers will have. And you're in control of that experience. It's easy to forget this during the rush of a busy day and before you know it, you and your teammates are delivering experiences that don't match up. When you and your entire team can get on brand and stay on brand, the foundations get laid to make selling easier - not just today, but in the future.

Master Series - Customer Experience.title: Delivering on Your Promises Requires Teamwork

Master Series - Customer Experience.description: It's on every corporate lunch room inspirational poster - "Team Work Makes the Dream Work." Handing tickets off to another advisor, setting up for when an advisor will be out, relying on others to make good notes, ... the list goes on when it comes to things that require good teamwork.
